title: Forward it untouched
description:
`receive` has two overloads: one for objects that must be copied (lvalues) and one for temporaries that may be moved from (rvalues).

Write `template <typename T> std::string relay(T&& widget)` that passes its argument on to `receive` **exactly as it arrived**: an lvalue stays an lvalue, an rvalue stays an rvalue.

Inside `relay`, `widget` has a name, so on its own it is always an lvalue. `std::forward<T>(widget)` restores the original category.
hints: The whole body is `return receive(std::forward<T>(widget));` (include `<utility>`). Without `std::forward`, every call would go to the lvalue overload.
unitTests:
TEST("an lvalue arrives as an lvalue") { Widget w{}; CHECK_EQ(relay(w), "copy"); const Widget c{}; CHECK_EQ(relay(c), "copy"); }
TEST("an rvalue arrives as an rvalue") { CHECK_EQ(relay(Widget{}), "move"); Widget w{}; CHECK_EQ(relay(std::move(w)), "move"); }
